Each entry must show the tool name with a concrete parameter set (resembling the documented schema, e.g. name + key:value args) AND a one-line justification stating why this tool was chosen over the tempting alternative. Only the six declared tools may appear; invented tools or invented/out-of-range parameters are format violations. The plan should end at the point where human coordination is required rather than fabricating a resolution.
evals.tone: Terse, operational incident-response register — an experienced on-call engineer writing an action plan under time pressure. Decisive but safety-aware; no hedging filler, no apologies, no customer-facing prose.

evals.expected: A strong answer must do all of the following. PHASE 1 — three GENUINELY orthogonal paradigms, not three variants of "stream-process then dedup in a KV store." Acceptable distinct angles include: (1) a unified batch+stream engine over one log with event-time windows and watermarks (e.g., Flink/Beam "one codebase, two runners" / Kappa-style replay), (2) an incremental materialized-view / set-semantics approach where credit is a deterministic FUNCTION of the current event set (e.g., a versioned fact table / Iceberg+merge or a differential-dataflow / incremental-recompute model that is inherently idempotent and supports revocation as a retraction), and (3) a bitemporal append-only ledger that records both event-time and ingest-time and derives credit by deterministic query, treating dedup as a property of keys rather than of processing. A weak answer's Phase 1 collapses two of these into the same paradigm (fake diversity) — the single most-penalized flaw, and the one the existing rate-limiter calibration fixture got dinged for. PHASE 2 — each weakness must bite on a SPECIFIC stated constraint: e.g., the pure-streaming/watermark approach must confront that clicks can arrive DAYS after the purchase, so any bounded watermark/allowed-lateness either drops valid late clicks or forces an unboundedly large state — a correctness-vs-state-size trap, not a generic "state is big" caveat; the recompute/materialized-view approach must confront cost/latency of re-deriving over 40B events on every late arrival (or must explain incremental retraction to avoid it); the bitemporal-ledger approach must confront that querying credit becomes an expensive as-of join and that revocation/refund correctness requires the query, not the write, to be the source of truth. EVALUATION MUST DRIVE SELECTION: Phase 3 must pick BECAUSE of a Phase-2 weakness (e.g., reject pure bounded-watermark streaming precisely because the days-late-click constraint breaks it), not merely assert a winner — evaluation theater (generic weaknesses that don't move the ranking) is a key flaw to detect. PREMATURE COMMITMENT: an answer that picks approach #1 regardless of its own evaluation, or that picks the most familiar (naive Kafka+Redis dedup) despite having identified its fatal flaw, fails. The FINAL DESIGN must concretely cover: (i) keying = deterministic dedup key on a content hash or natural (user, click_id, purchase_id) triple so at-least-once redelivery is idempotent (NOT a dedup that depends on processing order); (ii) handling days-late clicks WITHOUT a bounded watermark that drops them — typically by storing unmatched clicks/purchases in durable keyed state and matching on arrival from either side, with an explicit bound (the 30-day window) that lets state be reclaimed; (iii) batch/stream parity achieved by SHARED deterministic logic over the same event-time semantics (same code or same SQL/spec running on both, replay of the stream reproducing the batch) — NOT two independently-written pipelines hoped to agree; (iv) revocation handled as a first-class retraction/tombstone that propagates to downstream ledgers, with the 60-day refund window bounding retention; (v) two correctness-corrupting failure modes that are SPECIFIC, e.g., non-deterministic dedup under reprocessing (same triple credited twice because the dedup key included a processing timestamp or partition), watermark/lateness misconfiguration silently dropping valid late clicks, refund arriving after state was reclaimed so a revocation is lost, or batch and stream diverging because of floating-point/ordering/UDF nondeterminism. BACKTRACKING: bonus credit if, while detailing the chosen design, the model notices a wall (e.g., "pure streaming can't bound state for days-late clicks") and explicitly switches or grafts in another approach — and penalize if it bulldozes through a wall it earlier identified.
evals.format_spec: Three explicitly labeled phases in order (Phase 1: three named candidate paradigms; Phase 2: per-approach reasoning trace + one most-damaging weakness each; Phase 3: a selection justified by reference to the Phase-2 weaknesses, followed by a concrete final design covering data model, dedup/ordering, backfill/stream reconciliation, revocation, and the top correctness-corrupting failure modes). Selection in Phase 3 must cite the specific weaknesses from Phase 2. If a wall is hit while detailing the design, an explicit backtrack/switch must be stated rather than glossed over.
evals.tone: Senior data/distributed-systems engineer to a peer reviewing an architecture proposal: precise, decisive, candid about tradeoffs. No marketing language, no hedging filler, no closing upsell offers.
